annotations.shape: a two-hop Received chain whose timestamps run opposite to its header order (the last-listed hop claims 10:05, the first-listed claims 10:10) plus a Date claiming 10:00 -- TimeEvent conflict case 2 of 5, clock skew (D15)
annotations.phase_numbering: the design document's phases: 0 = the Phase 0 skeleton walker, 1 = the Phase 1 parser, 2 = routing and statuses, 3 = threading and time evidence -- every time.* fact here is phase 3
annotations.the_evidence: time.evidence rows are written in emailextract/timeevent.py's shape (see date_before_hops for the column meanings); the hop ordinals are the Received fields' header positions, and the chain sequence is fixed by those positions alone
annotations.the_policies: received_chain_header_order places the hops bottom-up (the last-listed Received is the first hop) and never re-sorts by timestamp -- which is exactly where this fixture's clocks disagree with the chain; header_date_claimed sorts the usable claims by their UTC; owner_manifest is the labelled override and is not evidence-ranked
annotations.the_conflicts: the hop pair is in conflict because the timestamps order the two hops opposite to their header positions (the definition of clock skew in D15); the Date pairs are cross-family claims naming different moments; time.evidence_conflicts is true and the pair list is non-empty
annotations.labels_are_typed: typed by a model from D2/D15 and the fixture's declared shape, never copied out of tests/support/timeline_ref.py or the library; labels_provenance is spec

value: the Date claims 2025-03-04T10:00:00Z while the first-listed hop claims 10:10:00Z: a claimed send time and a hop timestamp name different moments for the same message and no policy merges them
the Date claims 2025-03-04T10:00:00Z while the last-listed hop claims 10:05:00Z: two source families, two moments, nothing reconciles them
